summary.overview: The project has a rich agent guidance kernel, specialist routing, multi-layer validation, and CI enforcement. Session evidence is unavailable (0 eligible sessions), so all behavioral claims remain unobserved. Two structural gaps stand out: the learning-capture infrastructure has never produced episode records, and the delivery acceptance path beyond CI has no explicit owner or recovery route.

suggestions.title: Use the configured goal:verify script as a delivery acceptance gate
suggestions.reason: The project exposes npm run goal:verify and a ship loop, but the reviewed evidence does not show them exercised as a delivery acceptance boundary.
suggestions.nextStep: Run one bounded task through the full ship loop (goal start, phase implement, goal:verify, goal done) and confirm it produces verifiable acceptance evidence.
suggestions.validation: Confirm goal:verify passes and records a delivery decision tied to the current revision.

suggestions.title: Exercise the learning-loop script on the next repeated task
suggestions.reason: The project has npm run learn and .learnings/ infrastructure, but zero episode records were produced. The inspected capability exists without observed use.
suggestions.nextStep: After the next repeated friction or successful procedure, run npm run learn and confirm it captures a structured episode record.
suggestions.validation: Confirm .learnings/index.json contains at least one new episode entry with a reusable pattern.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md, 7 domain specialists with allow/deny globs, DESIGN.md visual contract, and progressive disclosure provide strong task routing. No session evidence to confirm exercised use.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Explicit command surface (dev/build/test/lint/clean), Node 24.x pinning, lockfile, and dev-healer hooks are present. Hook runtime behavior is unverified and paths are absolute.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Multi-layer lint (git, react, types, md, knip), 25 test files, pre-commit hooks, and CI with audit/test/build provide actionable feedback. No session evidence of exercised post-edit validation.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: CI runs on branch patterns and PRs to main, but no explicit acceptance evidence, branch protection, or recovery route is documented. Pre-commit is bypassable via environment variable.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: Learning scripts, .learnings directory, and graph-context infrastructure exist, but zero episode records and zero recurring candidates were produced. Detection has not been exercised.

findings.title: Learning detection infrastructure has never produced episode records
findings.reason: The project has learning-loop scripts, .learnings/ directory, active-prevention, and graph-context infrastructure, but the analyzer observed zero episode records and zero recurring candidates. The detection mechanism is present but has not been exercised, so repeated work and maintenance opportunities cannot be distinguished or routed.
expectedOutput: At least one structured episode record with goal, pattern, and validation fields populated.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Exercise the learning-loop detection on one bounded repeated task. Run npm run learn after a completed task episode and confirm it produces a structured episode record in .learnings/index.json.

## Validation

- Run npm run learn:status and confirm at least one episode record exists
- Confirm the record has a reusable pattern or friction attribution

findings.title: Delivery acceptance beyond CI has no explicit owner or recovery route
findings.reason: CI validates git standards, audit, tests, and build on branch pushes and PRs to main. However, no explicit acceptance decision (branch protection, required review, deployment approval) or recovery route (rollback command, restore procedure) is documented or mechanically enforced. A failed deployment has no owned recovery path.
expectedOutput: One explicit acceptance gate tied to the current revision and one owned rollback route.
findings.expectedArtifact: Delivery acceptance and recovery documentation or configuration
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Document or enforce one explicit delivery acceptance gate and one owned recovery route for the Vercel deployment. Keep the existing CI boundary.

## Validation

- Confirm the acceptance gate blocks or records a decision before production deployment
- Confirm one named recovery route (vercel rollback or equivalent) with an owner

findings.title: Dev-healer lifecycle hooks are configured but runtime behavior is unverified
findings.reason: The .agents/hooks.json configures PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks (context-injector, graphify-grep-enforcer, schema-validator, command-validator, episodic-capture) with absolute Windows paths. No test, fixture, or observed event sample confirms they execute correctly. Absolute paths reduce portability across machines.
expectedOutput: All configured dev-healer hooks report reachable and executable from the project root.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Add one smoke test or self-check that verifies the dev-healer hooks can execute (e.g., npm run hooks:status already exists). Confirm the hooks resolve their Python scripts without path errors.

## Validation

- Run npm run hooks:status and confirm all configured hooks report reachable
- Fix any absolute path that fails on a fresh checkout
